children: The concentration of the U.S. equity rally in a handful of technology companies poses a growing risk to broader markets, as weakness in artificial-intelligence-related stocks could trigger index losses, portfolio derisking and reduced investment in AI infrastructure, says Saxo Bank chief investment strategist Charu Chanana. However, an AI correction need not lead to a broader equity bear market. If corporate earnings remain resilient and economic growth holds up, investors could rotate into healthcare, selected financials and industrials, particularly companies with more attractive valuations, she adds. The key question is whether an AI-led correction triggers contagion or rotation, she says. Improving market breadth as tech stocks weaken would suggest capital is shifting among sectors, while sustained selling across industries could signal broader risk aversion, she adds.(jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
